title: Sheaves of modules on a scheme have enough injectives
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the underlying topological space of $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ has enough injectives: every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ admits a monomorphism $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I$ into an injective object $\mathcal I$ of $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. (Stacks states and proves this for an arbitrary ringed space, with functorial injective embeddings.)

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI (lemma-sheaves-modules-space); used in Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 01EO (literature/stacks-project/cohomology.tex, the paragraph defining $H^i(X,\mathcal F)$ by an injective resolution)

proof.text: *Injective hulls at the points.* For every $x\in X$ the stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives] applied to the ring $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $M=\mathcal F_x$, choose for each $x\in X$ an injective object $J_x$ of the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_{X,x})$ and an injective $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear map $j_x:\mathcal F_x\to J_x$ (the source takes the functorial embedding $j:\mathcal F_x\to J_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal F_x)$ of More on Algebra 01DD; only its existence is used here).

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI (lemma-sheaves-modules-space), proof, first sentence; More on Algebra, Lemma 01DD (more-algebra.tex, lemma-injectives-modules)

proof.text: *Each skyscraper $i_{x,*}J_x$ is injective in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$.* Fix $x$. The stalk functor $u:\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_{X,x})$, $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G_x$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_x$, is a functor between abelian categories ($\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $\Mod(\mathcal O_{X,x})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives]); it is additive, since $(\varphi+\psi)_x(s_x)=(\varphi_U(s)+\psi_U(s))_x=\varphi_x(s_x)+\psi_x(s_x)$ by the definition of stalk maps [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and it is exact: by [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (5) a sequence $\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules that is exact at $\mathcal F$ has $\mathcal F'_x\to\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal F''_x$ exact at $\mathcal F_x$, so $u$ carries short exact sequences to short exact sequences. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-skyscraper-stalk-adjunction] (1)-(3), $u$ has the right adjoint $u_*:A\mapsto i_{x,*}A$ (the bijection $\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,i_{x,*}A)\cong\Hom_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal G_x,A)$ natural in $\mathcal G$ and $A$). Hence by [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] $u_*$ carries the injective object $J_x$ of $\Mod(\mathcal O_{X,x})$ to an injective object $i_{x,*}J_x$ of $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. (The source: 'Hence it is clear that each $i_{x,*}I_x$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module (see Homology, Lemma 015Z or argue directly)'.)

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI, proof, second paragraph; Sheaves, Lemma 009C (sheaves.tex, lemma-stalk-skyscraper-adjoint); Homology, Lemma 015Z (homology.tex, lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives)

proof.text: *The product $\mathcal I=\prod_{x\in X}i_{x,*}J_x$ exists, is computed on sections, and is injective.* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], applied to the discrete diagram indexed by the set $X$ (the topological space $X$ viewed as a site whose objects are the opens), the family $(i_{x,*}J_x)_{x\in X}$ has a product $\mathcal I$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ with $\mathcal I(U)=\prod_{x\in X}(i_{x,*}J_x)(U)$, componentwise $\mathcal O_X(U)$-action and restriction maps, and projections $p_x:\mathcal I\to i_{x,*}J_x$ the coordinate projections. Since $(i_{x,*}J_x)(U)=0$ for $x\notin U$, $\mathcal I(U)=\prod_{x\in U}J_x$ (the sheaf $U\mapsto\prod_{x\in U}J_x$ of the source), with $r\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ acting by $r\cdot(a_x)_{x\in U}=(r_xa_x)_{x\in U}$ and restriction to $V\subseteq U$ the projection onto the factors $x\in V$. Every factor $i_{x,*}J_x$ is injective by step 2, and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is abelian [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $\mathcal I$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-product-injectives].

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI, proof: 'Note that I = prod_{x in X} i_{x,*}I_x is the product of the skyscraper sheaves' and 'Hence the injectivity of I follows from Homology, Lemma 0137 (lemma-product-injectives)'; the sheaf U -> prod_{x in U} I_x: Sheaves, Examples 006X, 007R

proof.text: *The map $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I$.* For each $x$ let $\alpha^x:\mathcal F\to i_{x,*}J_x$ be the morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules that corresponds to $j_x:\mathcal F_x\to J_x$ under the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-module-skyscraper-stalk-adjunction] (2): $\alpha^x_U(s)=j_x(s_x)$ for $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ if $x\in U$, and $\alpha^x_U=0$ if $x\notin U$. By the universal property of the product (step 3, [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]) there is a unique morphism $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I$ with $p_x\circ\alpha=\alpha^x$ for all $x$; on sections, $\alpha_U(s)=(j_x(s_x))_{x\in U}\in\prod_{x\in U}J_x$, which is the canonical map of the source.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI, proof: 'There is a canonical map F -> I given by mapping s in F(U) to prod_{x in U} j(s_x)'

proof.text: *$\alpha$ is a monomorphism.* Let $U\subseteq X$ be open and $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ with $\alpha_U(s)=0$. Then $j_x(s_x)=0$ for every $x\in U$, hence $s_x=0=0_x$ for every $x\in U$ because $j_x$ is injective (step 1). The underlying sheaf of sets of the $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $s$ and $0\in\mathcal F(U)$, having the same germ at every point of $U$, are equal [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sections-determined-by-germs]. Thus every $\alpha_U$ is injective. Then $\alpha$ is a monomorphism of $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$: if $a,b:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ satisfy $\alpha\circ a=\alpha\circ b$, then $\alpha_U(a_U(t))=\alpha_U(b_U(t))$ for all $U$ and $t\in\mathcal G(U)$, so $a_U=b_U$ for all $U$ and $a=b$.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI, proof: 'This map is injective, see Sheaves, Lemma 0079 (lemma-sheaf-subset-stalks)'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I$ is a monomorphism (step 5) into an injective object (step 3) of $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$. As $\mathcal F$ was arbitrary, $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ has enough injectives in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions].
